viewpoints.claim: Separate elements with space, a background shift, a shadow or striping before reaching for a border; too many borders make a design busy.

source.author: Adam Wathan & Steve Schoger
source.work: Refactoring UI
source.quote: Borders are a great way to distinguish two elements from one another, but using too many of them can make your design feel busy and cluttered.

prefers: Separate groups with space
Shift the background colour or add a shadow instead of a line
Zebra-stripe table rows instead of ruling them
forbids: Use a 1px border as the default grouping device
Wrap a nav in a panel that only needs to recede
Rule every table row with a border when striping would do

measure.what: For every text node, count ancestors with a visible border, non-none box-shadow or outline; report max nesting depth and bordered boxes per viewport.
measure.mustFail: Card with border:1px solid inside a bordered section inside a bordered page container, all only grouping (depth 3).
measure.mustPass: Same DOM; outer two borders replaced by margin-top:32px and a #f7f7f8 band; only the card keeps its border (depth 1).

exceptions: Form inputs and the one object a person acts on keep their border
Keylines that make disconnected content feel connected
Decorative borders as style once the count is low

viewpoints.claim: Use the lightest separator that works: more space first, then a keyline or background band, and a box only for the object that is acted on.

source.author: Adam Wathan & Steve Schoger; Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: Refactoring UI (fewer-borders tactic); 7 Rules for Creating Gorgeous UI, Part 1

prefers: Separate with whitespace by default
Add a keyline or background band only when space alone fails
Box only the object a person acts on
forbids: Reach for a card or border first

measure.what: Between sibling groups, record which separator is used: gap at least 2x the inner gap (space), hr or border-bottom (line), bordered or shadowed wrapper (box); report the inner/outer gap ratio.
measure.mustFail: Three sibling groups each in a bordered box, 8px between boxes and 8px inside them.
measure.mustPass: Same groups, no wrappers, 8px inside and 32px between.

exceptions: Dense data such as tables where zebra stripes or keylines are used
Interactive cards that are the unit of action

viewpoints.claim: Squint: the most important thing must catch the eye first and the least important last; one element dominates each screen.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: 4 Rules for Intuitive UX
source.quote: If you squint your eyes, the Most Important Thing should catch your eye first – and the least important elements should catch your eye last.

prefers: Give each screen one dominant element
Emphasize the most-used functionality
De-emphasize, hide or remove the rarely used
forbids: Make the primary action grey and unnoticeable beside a bigger, brighter Help
Render two identical grey buttons where one is the main action

measure.what: Given a declared primary action, score every interactive element as area x contrast x font-weight factor; the declared primary must rank first, and no set of buttons may sit within 10% of each other.
measure.mustFail: Submit as a grey 12px text button, Help as a 16px filled blue button.
measure.mustPass: Submit filled in brand colour at 16px, Help a plain text link.

exceptions: Page titles are the only element styled all-out up-pop
A browsing page such as a gallery may have no single most important thing

viewpoints.claim: Build text hierarchy from two or three colours and two weights; use size only for real levels.

source.author: Steve Schoger
source.work: Little UI Details (tweet, 19 Sep 2017)
source.quote: Font size isn't always the best way to emphasize or de-emphasize text, try using color and font weight instead

prefers: Use primary, secondary and tertiary text greys
Use two font weights
Style section labels small, bold, uppercase and softer
forbids: Give every level of importance its own font-size
Render labels as big bold headings

measure.what: Count distinct computed text colours and font-weights; check that secondary text differs from primary by colour or weight, not only by size.
measure.mustFail: Six text levels realised as six font-sizes, all #000, all weight 400.
measure.mustPass: Three sizes, three greys, two weights.

exceptions: Display and marketing headlines where size is the hierarchy
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Maybe outside content: applies to the heading and meta-text blocks, not to charts, tables of values, product tiles or form fields.

viewpoints.claim: To emphasize, quiet the competitors as much as you loudify the hero; never stack every up-pop property on non-title elements.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: 7 Rules for Creating Gorgeous UI, Part 2
source.quote: If an element needs emphasis, apply BOTH up-pop and down-pop styles — but slightly MORE up-pop.

prefers: Set big numbers light and lower-contrast
Set small labels uppercase and bold
Make the competitor quieter rather than the hero louder
forbids: Stack big, bold, bright and uppercase on any element that is not the page title

measure.what: Flag text at 2x body size or more that is also font-weight 700+, full contrast and uppercase, when it is not the page h1.
measure.mustFail: Stat card: number 48px/800/#000, label 18px/800/#000/uppercase.
measure.mustPass: Number 48px/300/#334; label 12px/700/uppercase/#777 with letter-spacing.

exceptions: The page title may be all-out up-pop
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Maybe on content, workspace and transaction: applies where one element must lead (page title, primary action), not to uniform text or rows.

viewpoints.claim: On a coloured background, soften text by hand-picking a tint of the background hue, never by neutral grey or reduced opacity.

source.author: Steve Schoger
source.work: Little UI Details (tweet, 12 Jun 2017)
source.quote: Pure grey text always looks 'off' on a colored background. A quick fix is to saturate your text with a bit of the background hue.

prefers: Pick a text colour that shares the background hue at reduced contrast
Rotate the hue toward a brighter neighbour for perceived brightness
forbids: Put zero-saturation grey text on a saturated background
Soften text on colour with opacity below 1 or an rgba alpha

measure.what: For text whose effective background has HSL saturation above 30%: fail if text saturation is under 5% with lightness 20–80%, or if text opacity or alpha is below 1.
measure.mustFail: background:#2563eb; color:#9ca3af
measure.mustPass: background:#2563eb; color:#bfdbfe

exceptions: White and near-black text are not grey for this rule
Disabled states are a separate convention
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Maybe everywhere: applies only where text sits on a coloured background (hero bands, banners, badges, coloured panels).

viewpoints.claim: Tint the neutral scale toward the brand hue and never use pure black for text.

source.author: Steve Schoger
source.work: Little UI Details (tweet, 19 Mar 2018)
source.quote: 'Grey' doesn't have to mean Grey™. Try saturating your greys with a bit of blue or brown for a cooler or warmer feel.

prefers: Tint the grey scale toward the brand hue
Raise saturation at the light and dark ends of the scale
forbids: Use #000 for text
Use pure zero-saturation greys as the whole neutral palette

measure.what: Count text, border and background colours with saturation 0 and lightness under 15%, and the share of neutral swatches with saturation exactly 0.
measure.mustFail: color:#000 body text on #fff
measure.mustPass: color:#1f2937

exceptions: It does not always work; worth a trial
High-contrast or accessibility modes and print

viewpoints.claim: Start with far more breathing room than feels necessary and remove it until it works; browser-default spacing is the largest mistake.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: 7 Rules for Creating Gorgeous UI, Part 1
source.quote: To make UI that looks designed, add a lot of breathing room. … Sometimes a ridiculous amount.

prefers: Pad controls at least the text's own height
Space list and nav items twice the text height
Separate groups with much more space than sits within them
forbids: Ship browser-default spacing with everything smashed toward the top

measure.what: Ratio of vertical padding to font-size on list items, nav items and buttons; ratio of gap between groups to gap within a group.
measure.mustFail: Nav links padding:2px 4px at 14px; sections margin:0.
measure.mustPass: Nav links padding:12px 16px; sections margin-top:48px.

exceptions: Dense professional, interaction-heavy tools may compress, but spacing must stay consistent
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on workspace, whose screens want density for repeated work; maybe on data and transaction around the header and group gaps, not inside tables or fields.

viewpoints.claim: Draw every margin, padding and gap from one scale, and make space between groups clearly larger than space within them.

source.author: Steve Schoger
source.work: Little UI Details (tweet, 13 Jul 2017)
source.quote: Using multiples to define your spacing is a great way to achieve vertical rhythm and provides a formula to justify your choices

prefers: Take spacing from a ladder of multiples of 4
Make between-group gaps larger than within-group gaps
forbids: Use one-off values such as 13px or 27px
Use equal gaps across a group boundary

measure.what: Collect all computed margin, padding and gap values above 0; report distinct values and how many are off a 4px grid; compare label-to-field gap with field-to-next-label gap.
measure.mustFail: Paddings {7, 11, 13, 18, 27}; label to input 12px and input to next label 12px.
measure.mustPass: Paddings {8, 12, 16, 24, 32}; label to input 4px, field to field 24px.

exceptions: Optical adjustments on icons and hanging punctuation sit a pixel or two off-scale

viewpoints.claim: Let content dictate its own width and the layout follow; do not stretch components because the screen grew.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: Why Beginning Designers Don't Need Grids, Type Scales, or Color Theory
source.quote: The hassle with grids is that they force the content into a specific width. Content should always dictate it's own width … and the layout should follow suit.

prefers: On mobile align to three rulers: 16px left, centre, 16px right
Keep content at fixed sizes such as a 72px thumbnail
forbids: Stretch every element wider because the phone got wider
Size components by percentage so they shrink below their content's need

measure.what: At 360–414px viewport, every content edge sits at 16px (or one consistent gutter) from the viewport edge and nothing overflows horizontally.
measure.mustFail: Page with padding:0 at 375px whose text touches the edge, or a width:8.33% column producing a 26px cell.
measure.mustPass: 16px gutters, fixed 72px thumbnail, text fills the rest.

exceptions: Strict grids for posters and websites where the artistry of the composition matters more than the information
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on data, where dashboards fill the width on purpose; maybe on marketing, content, workspace and shop for forms, cards and text blocks that should not stretch.

viewpoints.claim: Use about four font sizes from a fixed scale; reuse the default size for body, menus, lists and controls.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: The Responsive Website Font Size Guidelines
source.quote: Even the most interaction-heavy pages can typically look just fine with about 4 font sizes total.

prefers: Use header, default, secondary (default minus 2px) and one wildcard size
Reuse the default size across body, menus, lists and controls
forbids: Invent a new size per component
Apply a strict modular or golden-ratio scale to responsive pages

measure.what: Count distinct computed font-size values on visible text per viewport and how many fall outside the declared scale.
measure.mustPass: {12,14,16,24} — four values, all on the scale.

exceptions: Sizes must stay distinguishable, so large text may step many points apart
Marketing pages may add a display size

viewpoints.claim: Body copy at 16px or more with 1.5 line height; inputs at 16px or more on mobile.

source.author: Steve Schoger
source.work: Little UI Details (tweet, 1 Jun 2017)
source.quote: If in doubt, 16px font with 1.5 line height is pretty good safe for body copy.

prefers: Set body at 16px or more, secondary about 2px smaller
Set inputs at 16px or more on mobile
Set text-heavy desktop pages at 18–24px
forbids: Set body text under 16px on phones
Set inputs under 16px on iOS

measure.what: At a 375px viewport, computed font-size of paragraph text and of input, textarea and select; line-height divided by font-size for paragraphs.
measure.mustFail: p{font-size:13px;line-height:1.1} input{font-size:14px}
measure.mustPass: p{font-size:16px;line-height:1.5} input{font-size:16px}

exceptions: Interaction-heavy desktop pages may go to 14px
Captions sit 2px under body by design
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on data, whose numbers and tables run dense; maybe on marketing, workspace and shop for their paragraphs and inputs only.

viewpoints.claim: Line height is proportional: tighten it as text gets larger and loosen it as lines get longer.

source.author: Steve Schoger
source.work: Little UI Details (tweet, 27 Feb 2018)
source.quote: 1.5 may work great for body copy, but as text gets larger, your line-height should get tighter.

prefers: Set headings around 1.1–1.25 and body around 1.5
Give longer measures more leading
forbids: Inherit one line-height:1.5 onto 40px headlines
Set line-height:1 on paragraphs

measure.what: For each text element compute line-height divided by font-size; the ratio on headlines at 2x body or larger must be smaller than the body ratio.
measure.mustFail: h1{font-size:40px;line-height:1.6} p{line-height:1.6}
measure.mustPass: h1{line-height:1.15} p{line-height:1.5}

exceptions: Single-line headings where line height is invisible
No one-size-fits-all number; assert direction only
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on data, workspace and transaction, which have no large display type or long lines; maybe on shop for product headings and descriptions.

viewpoints.claim: Cap paragraph measure at 50–75 characters per line and do not let it fall under about 30.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: The Responsive Website Font Size Guidelines
source.quote: Body text should have 50-75 characters per line.

prefers: Cap paragraph width with max-width in ch
forbids: Stretch paragraphs across a 1440px viewport

measure.what: For each p with 3 or more rendered lines, estimate characters per line from element width divided by average glyph advance.
measure.mustFail: A p 1200px wide at 16px type, about 150 characters per line.
measure.mustPass: Same paragraph with max-width:65ch.

exceptions: Tables and forms are not paragraph text
Blurbs under 3 lines are not measured
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on data, workspace and transaction, which carry no long paragraphs; maybe on marketing and shop for body copy and product descriptions.

viewpoints.claim: Pair uppercase text with positive letter-spacing; track large bold headlines slightly negative.

source.author: Steve Schoger
source.work: Little UI Details (tweet, 31 May 2017)
source.quote: All-caps can sometimes be difficult to read. Consider using letter-spacing to give your text a little more room to breathe

prefers: Pair text-transform:uppercase with about 0.05em letter-spacing and a slightly smaller size
Track large bold headlines about -1%
forbids: Leave uppercase labels at letter-spacing:normal

measure.what: For text with text-transform:uppercase or all-caps content of 4 or more letters, fail if computed letter-spacing is normal or 0.
measure.mustFail: .label{text-transform:uppercase}
measure.mustPass: .label{text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.05em}

exceptions: Logos and wordmarks
Single-letter avatars
Monospace text
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Maybe everywhere: applies only where uppercase labels, eyebrows or table headers or large bold headlines occur.

viewpoints.claim: Counterbalance heavy icons beside text by giving them a softer colour than the text; keep one icon set.

source.author: Steve Schoger
source.work: Little UI Details (tweet, 8 Jun 2017)
source.quote: If I am using icons that have more weight than the text, I typically make the icons slightly lighter than the text for inactive states

prefers: Colour inactive icons a lighter grey than their text
Use one consistent icon set and stroke weight
forbids: Set icons at full black beside 70% grey text
Mix outline and filled icon families in one bar

measure.what: For each inline svg or icon adjacent to text, compare its fill or stroke contrast against the background with the text's; the icon's must not exceed the text's.
measure.mustFail: Nav items with text #374151 and icons #000.
measure.mustPass: Same nav with icons #9ca3af.

exceptions: Active or selected state where the icon takes the brand colour
Icon-only buttons with nothing to balance against
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on content and transaction, where icons beside text are rare; maybe elsewhere for nav, toolbars and icon-labelled lists.

viewpoints.claim: Light comes from above: shadows get a slight positive vertical offset, raised things are lighter on top, inset things darker.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: 7 Rules for Creating Gorgeous UI, Part 1
source.quote: Light comes from the sky so frequently and consistently that for it to come from below actually looks freaky.

prefers: Give box-shadows a positive y offset and near-zero x offset
Shade inset elements darker at the top and raised elements lighter at the top
forbids: Use negative y offsets that light from below
Use heavy x offsets
Use one huge unblurred shadow

measure.what: Parse every computed box-shadow; fail any non-inset shadow with offset-y below 0 or |offset-x| greater than offset-y.
measure.mustFail: box-shadow: 0 -4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.2)
measure.mustPass: box-shadow: 0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.2)

exceptions: Flat design with no shadows at all
A top bar's shadow cast below it is still y-positive
Sticky footers casting upward are a known trade-off the source does not bless
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on content, which has no raised surfaces; maybe elsewhere where cards, menus or modals cast shadows.

viewpoints.claim: Use a fixed ladder of about five shadows mapped to element kinds: button, dropdown, panel, modal; larger shadow means closer.

source.author: Steve Schoger (attendee notes by ynotdraw)
source.work: Practical Solutions to Common UI Design Problems, CSS Day 2019
source.quote: use multiple shadows, larger shadow, closer it feels to the user.

prefers: Define about five shadow tokens and map each element kind to a rung
forbids: Give a modal a smaller shadow than a card
Write ad-hoc shadows per component

measure.what: Collect distinct non-inset box-shadow strings, expect at most 5–6; rank by blur plus offset; the dialog or modal shadow must rank above card and button shadows.
measure.mustFail: 14 distinct shadows; modal 0 1px 2px, card 0 20px 40px.
measure.mustPass: Four tokens with the modal on the top rung.

exceptions: Flat systems with no shadows
Elevation carried by colour, lighter objects feel closer
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on content, which has no raised surfaces; maybe elsewhere where buttons, dropdowns, panels or modals are elevated.

viewpoints.claim: Design in greyscale first, then add one accent hue with purpose; vary by saturation and brightness, not by more hues.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: 7 Rules for Creating Gorgeous UI, Part 1
source.quote: Design black and white first … Add color last, and even then, only with purpose.

prefers: Use greyscale plus one or two accent hues
Vary colour by saturation and brightness within a hue
forbids: Use complementary or triadic colour-theory palettes as UI palettes
Give each section its own hue

measure.what: Cluster computed colours with saturation above 25% by hue within 15 degrees; count clusters, excluding declared semantic states such as error, success and warning.
measure.mustFail: Seven hue clusters on a settings screen: blue nav, green cards, purple buttons, orange tags.
measure.mustPass: One brand hue plus neutrals plus a declared red for errors.

exceptions: Sporty, flashy or cartoony brands that need a colour-fluent designer
Data-visualisation palettes
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Maybe except shop: applies to the UI chrome palette, not to brand imagery, chart series or status colours.

viewpoints.claim: Keep few strong left edges, right-align comparable numbers with tabular figures, and hang punctuation so edges line up.

source.author: Steve Schoger
source.work: Little UI Details (tweet, 15 Jun 2017)
source.quote: Aligning text is an easy way to clean up your design and make your content much more scannable.

prefers: Keep few, strong left edges
Right-align numeric columns with tabular figures
Hang bullets, icons and punctuation so text edges align
forbids: Align a right-aligned image to ragged left-aligned text
Centre columns of numbers

measure.what: Count distinct left-edge x positions of text blocks in a container at 1px tolerance; for td cells matching a number or currency pattern, text-align must be right or end and tabular figures must be set.
measure.mustFail: Price column text-align:left with no tnum; card title, body and button at x = 24, 27 and 31.
measure.mustPass: Price column right-aligned with tnum; all three at x = 24.

exceptions: IDs, ZIP codes and phone numbers stay left-aligned
Centred layouts under 3 lines
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on marketing, which has no columns of comparable numbers; maybe on content, shop and transaction for tables, prices and order summaries.

viewpoints.claim: Centre text only when there are fewer than three lines, and rarely even then; body text is left-aligned.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: 100 Things a UX/UI Designer Should Know
source.quote: When to center text — Only when there are fewer than 3 lines of it. And, even then, rarely.

prefers: Left-align body text
Centre only short headings or empty-state lines
forbids: Centre paragraphs

measure.what: For every block with text-align:center, count rendered line boxes from Range client rects; fail at 3 or more.
measure.mustFail: A six-line centred paragraph.
measure.mustPass: Same text left-aligned, or a two-line centred subtitle.

exceptions: Poetry, quotes or hero copy the project explicitly commits to
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on data and workspace, which do not centre text blocks; maybe on marketing, shop and transaction for heroes, banners and confirmation messages.

viewpoints.claim: One filled brand-colour button per view; secondaries outlined, tertiaries as text, destructive actions quiet with a confirmation step.

source.author: Steve Schoger
source.work: Little UI Details (tweet, 2 Aug 2017)
source.quote: You want your primary button to stand out much more than your secondary / danger actions.

prefers: Fill exactly one button per view or dialog in the brand colour
Outline secondary actions and set tertiary actions as text
Keep destructive actions quiet unless they are the primary job
forbids: Let a green button compete with the primary
Put a big red Delete beside a small Save
Colour every link brand blue

measure.what: Classify buttons as filled, outlined or text from computed style; fail if a view or dialog has more than one filled button of distinct hues, or a delete-labelled button is filled while the confirming action is not.
measure.mustFail: Dialog with filled blue Save and filled red Delete.
measure.mustPass: Filled Save, text-link Delete.

exceptions: Segmented or toggle groups
Toolbars of equal-weight actions
A page whose only job is the destructive action, where red is primary
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Maybe on content and data: applies to the few action bars and toolbars they carry, not to reading or chart areas.

viewpoints.claim: Let values carry their own format; when a label is needed it is small, soft and subordinate to the value.

source.author: Steve Schoger (attendee notes by ynotdraw)
source.work: Practical Solutions to Common UI Design Problems, CSS Day 2019
source.quote: Most of the time you don't need a label at all!

prefers: Show values that carry their own format, such as $29 or a city name, without a prefix
Make any needed label small, softer and subordinate
Design the UI independently of the database fields
forbids: Dump Field: value pairs where the label outweighs the value

measure.what: Detect dt/dd pairs and Word: prefixes; when present, the label's size x weight x contrast must not exceed the value's.
measure.mustPass: dt 12px/600/#888 uppercase, dd 16px/500/#111.

exceptions: Form inputs need labels for accessibility
Data that is ambiguous without a name, such as two dates or two counts
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on marketing and content, which show few labelled values, and on transaction, where form fields need their labels; maybe on shop for spec lists.

viewpoints.claim: Put an overlay, scrim, box, blur or floor fade between photo and text, and test legibility at every viewport.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: 7 Rules for Creating Gorgeous UI, Part 2
source.quote: There are only a few ways of reliably and beautifully overlaying text on images

prefers: Place an overlay, gradient or scrim between the photo and the text
Test legibility at every screen size
forbids: Set raw text on an un-darkened photo
Rely on a photo's out-of-focus area that moves when the image changes

measure.what: For text stacked over an img or background-image, sample painted pixels behind each glyph box from a screenshot; fail if minimum contrast is under 3:1 or the contrast spread across the box exceeds a threshold.
measure.mustFail: White 18px text over a bright sky and sea photo with no overlay.
measure.mustPass: Same with a linear-gradient(rgba(0,0,0,.45),…) overlay.

exceptions: Decorative text that is not read, such as watermarks
A fixed, dark, low-contrast image
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on data, workspace and transaction, which do not set text on photos; maybe on content and shop for header images and banners.

viewpoints.claim: Meet 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for headlines, prefer soft backgrounds with dark text, and never convey status by colour alone.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: 100 Things a UX/UI Designer Should Know
source.quote: The WCAG recommended contrast ratio for body text — 4.5:1 to meet AA standards

prefers: Style coloured badges as a soft background with dark text
Pair every colour state with an icon or label
forbids: Set white text on yellow, green or red fills that fail 4.5:1
Convey status by colour only

measure.what: Standard contrast ratio of computed text colour against effective background at 4.5:1 or 3:1 by size; status elements must carry a non-colour signal such as text or an icon.
measure.mustFail: background:#22c55e; color:#fff 12px badge, about 2.2:1.
measure.mustPass: background:#dcfce7; color:#166534.

exceptions: Disabled controls
Logos
Incidental text, per WCAG itself

viewpoints.claim: Style form controls instead of shipping browser defaults, keep one corner radius, and give inputs 40–48px of height.

source.author: Steve Schoger (attendee notes by ynotdraw)
source.work: Practical Solutions to Common UI Design Problems, CSS Day 2019
source.quote: Don't use default radio buttons and checkboxes. Create your own!

prefers: Style checkboxes, radios and the select arrow
Use one corner radius across the screen
Make inputs 40 or 48px tall with an off-white background on a white page
forbids: Ship browser-default checkbox, radio or select rendering
Mix radii such as 2, 4, 8 and 999 on one screen

measure.what: Checkbox, radio and select with appearance auto and no accent-color count as default; count distinct border-radius values on controls and cards excluding pills; flag inputs under 40px tall at desktop.
measure.mustFail: Native checkboxes, radii {2,3,6,10}, inputs 28px tall.
measure.mustPass: accent-color or custom controls, radius {4}, inputs 40px.

exceptions: Content-heavy sites where native controls are a deliberate accessibility choice
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on content, which has no form controls; maybe on marketing, data and shop for sign-up boxes, filters and quantity pickers.

viewpoints.claim: Put a control where its effect will appear, not where there happens to be room.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: 4 Rules for Intuitive UX
source.quote: Put interface elements where they effect change. … when a user wants to make a change to the system, they will unwittingly glance at where that change will happen.

prefers: Place Add at the end or top of the list it adds to
Anchor the control if the list can grow off-screen
forbids: Bury actions in a menu or floating button where nobody will look
Copy a floating action button because a respected company did

measure.what: Given a declared control-to-target pairing, measure pixel distance between the control box and the target region and whether both are in the viewport at once; fail beyond a signed threshold or off-screen.
measure.mustFail: New playlist in a top-right kebab menu with the list at the bottom-left.
measure.mustPass: The button as the last row of the list.

exceptions: When the end of the list is unreliable, the nearest logical place such as the top
Global actions belong in global chrome
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on marketing, whose single call to action has no local effect; maybe on content, workspace, shop and transaction for filters, inline edits and summaries.

viewpoints.claim: Before a dropdown, try a switch, segmented control, radios, cards, typeahead, calendar, text input or stepper.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: 4 Rules for Intuitive UX
source.quote: Any time you feel tempted to use a dropdown, ask yourself if one of these 12 controls is better instead. … dropdowns are pretty much the worst control.

prefers: Use a switch, checkbox or segmented button for two options
Use radios, segmented buttons or cards for two to five options
Use typeahead for long lists, a calendar or text input for dates, a stepper for counts
forbids: Use a select for five or fewer options
Use three selects for a date
Ship a 195-country select without search on mobile

measure.what: For each select: fail at 5 or fewer options unless committed as a rarely changed default; fail 2–3 adjacent selects with day, month, year options; flag over 30 options at 375px with no typeahead.
measure.mustFail: A select with Yes/No; date of birth as three selects.
measure.mustPass: A switch; input type=date or a masked text field.

exceptions: Users rarely need to change the default value
There are very few options
The user is not on mobile
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on marketing and content, which carry no choice controls; maybe on data for filter and range pickers.

viewpoints.claim: Touch targets are at least 44×44; inputs and the buttons beside them share one height of 40 or 48px.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: 100 Things a UX/UI Designer Should Know
source.quote: The minimum tap target size on both iOS and Android — On iOS: 44x44pt. On Android: 48x48pt.

prefers: Give touch viewports hit areas of 44×44 or more
Match button height to the inputs beside it
forbids: Use 26px-wide grid cells as targets
Make buttons shorter than the inputs they sit beside

measure.what: At 375px, getBoundingClientRect of every a, button, input and role=button: fail under 44 in width or height (under 24 for inline text links); in a form row, button and input heights within 2px.
measure.mustFail: 32px icon buttons; a 36px input beside a 44px button.
measure.mustPass: 44px all round.

exceptions: Inline text links in running prose
Dense desktop-only tools if the project commits to no touch

viewpoints.claim: Design the first-load and empty states with sample data or an example, a message and a call to action; never a blank page.

source.author: Erik D. Kennedy
source.work: 4 Rules for Intuitive UX
source.quote: Use the 'first load' experience to provide sample data, showing by example what the properly-working app will look like

prefers: Show a designed empty state with message, example and call to action
Seed sample data on first load
Show examples rather than descriptions
forbids: Show a totally blank page on first load
Show a table header with no rows and no message

measure.what: In the journey's declared empty state, find list or table containers with 0 data children; require a visible sentence inside or adjacent and at least one actionable element.
measure.mustFail: A table with thead only.
measure.mustPass: Same plus an empty-state block with copy and a Create the first… button.

exceptions: Zero-hit search results need a message but no sample data
Transient loading states
viewpoints.kindsWhy: No on marketing, content and transaction, which never render empty; maybe on shop for no-results and empty-cart states.

viewpoints.claim: Resolve outcome, system and interaction before visual design; pixels that do not serve a stated job are art, not design.

source.author: Paul Adams
source.work: The dribbblisation of design (Intercom, 2013)
source.quote: The grid, font, colour, and aesthetic style are irrelevant if the other three layers haven't been resolved first. … that's art not design.

prefers: Work top-down: outcome, then system, then interactions, then visual design
Frame every problem as a job: when, I want to, so I can
Prototype with real data
forbids: Ship flat PNGs and pixel-perfect executions that solve no stated problem
Redesign others' products without their constraints
Apply interchangeable styling regardless of the product

measure.what: Do the journey and understanding files exist and name the actor's job before the screen is measured, and does the visual layer serve that job? A machine checks the first; a person the second.

exceptions: Executing beautiful looking things is an important skill; the visual layer is last, not worthless
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Maybe everywhere: a process check on whether the screen serves a stated job, reviewable only when the brief is available.

viewpoints.claim: Design for how people filter, find meaning, act in time and remember: fewer choices, chunking, one salient element, recognition, clear defaults, used ethically.

source.author: Growth.Design (Dan Benoni, Louis-Xavier Lavallée)
source.work: 106 Cognitive Biases & Principles That Affect Your UX
source.quote: Every time users interact with your product, they: filter the information, seek the meaning of it, act within a given time, store bits of the interaction in their memories.

prefers: Offer fewer choices per step
Chunk forms and information
Make exactly one element salient in a group
Favour recognition over recall and set a clear default
forbids: Use the same levers as dark patterns

measure.what: Count interactive choices visible in one step; count elements carrying the accent hue within a group, expecting exactly one; proximity and target size are covered by the spacing and tap-target entries.
measure.mustFail: 24 equal buttons in one step; all six plan cards highlighted.
measure.mustPass: Five buttons plus a more control; one plan card highlighted.

exceptions: The catalogue is descriptive, not a rulebook; each principle carries an ethics caveat
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Maybe on content, data and workspace: applies to their choice points and defaults, not to reading or repeated work.
